rationale: The literature establishes that PSMD12 haploinsufficiency is the central pathogenic mechanism of Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome (STISS), whether caused by intragenic truncating/loss-of-function single-nucleotide variants or deletions encompassing PSMD12. However, the claim that there is 'no robust phenotypic divergence' between 17q24.2 microdeletions and intragenic truncating variants faces clear contradiction: 17q24.2 microdeletions frequently encompass neighboring morbid genes, such as BPTF (which independently causes syndromic developmental delay and postnatal microcephaly), as well as complex topologically associating domain (TAD) structures. Studies specifically note that certain prenatal manifestations and severe multi-system dysmorphic features appear preferentially or exclusively in individuals harboring multi-gene 17q24 microdeletions rather than isolated intragenic PSMD12 variants.

evidence.text: STISS is characterized by PSMD12 haploinsufficiency across patients harboring either truncating single-nucleotide variants or copy-number variant deletions encompassing PSMD12, both producing clinical neurodevelopmental phenotypes and variable expressivity.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome: expanding the clinical and molecular phenotype
source.quote: We report 24 additional unrelated patients with STISS with various truncating single nucleotide variants or copy-number variant deletions involving PSMD12.

evidence.text: PSMD12 haploinsufficiency drives STISS across inherited or de novo truncating variants; however, literature review indicates that multiple prenatal findings have been reported specifically in 17q24 microdeletions encompassing PSMD12 rather than in isolated intragenic variants.

source.quote: Proposed novel genotype-phenotype correlations based on new literature information on the region include the role of PSMD12 and BPTF, the genes recently associated with syndromic neurodevelopmental disorders, and a possible role of the complex topologically associated domain structure of the region, which may explain some of the phenotypic discrepancies observed between patients with similar but not identical deletions.

evidence.text: BPTF haploinsufficiency on 17q24.2 independently causes syndromic developmental and speech delay, postnatal microcephaly, and dysmorphic features, demonstrating that larger deletions covering 17q24.2 incorporate distinct clinical features from contiguous gene disruption.

source.title: Haploinsufficiency of the chromatin remodeler BPTF causes syndromic developmental and speech delay, postnatal microcephaly, and dysmorphic features
source.quote: The BPTF variants were found in unrelated individuals aged between 2.1 and 13 years, who manifest variable degrees of developmental delay/intellectual disability (10/10), speech delay (10/10), postnatal microcephaly (7/9), and dysmorphic features (9/10).

conflicts: While intragenic PSMD12 loss-of-function variants and microdeletions both manifest the core STISS neurodevelopmental phenotype through haploinsufficiency, multi-gene 17q24 microdeletions exhibit additional phenotypic divergence, including prenatal presentations and distinct dysmorphic features resulting from contiguous gene loss (such as BPTF) and regional TAD reorganization.

new_directions.question_text: To what extent do TAD disruptions and contiguous deletion of BPTF explain the severity and presence of microcephaly or prenatal findings in 17q24.2 microdeletions versus pure PSMD12 intragenic truncations?
new_directions.rationale: Systematically comparing high-resolution breakpoint-mapped 17q24 deletions against isolated PSMD12 SNVs will delineate true PSMD12 monogenic traits from contiguous gene syndrome features.
